title_th: การรับพัสดุ
recycles: telling the time and 'in ten minutes'
clarification: 'Sorry, could you say that again?'
thanking and closing a short exchange
register: Casual-polite, fast and transactional — the driver is in a hurry, so short clear sentences win

Leave it at the front desk.
targets.why_it_matters_here: Thai speakers unrelease final stops, so 'sign' comes out as 'sigh' and 'box' as 'bok'. At a doorstep the driver has 30 seconds: if 'This isn't mine' loses its final /n/ and /d/ sounds, it can be heard as 'This is mine' — and you have just signed for someone else's parcel and become responsible for it.

words_in_context: I'll be down in five minutes.
The last four digits are six zero one nine.
targets.why_it_matters_here: The whole delivery hangs on one number. If 'fourteen' is heard as 'forty' over a crackly intercom, your parcel goes to a flat on another floor and the app says 'delivered'. Stress the second syllable and finish the /n/ in -teen.

model_dialogues.label: A standard doorstep delivery — confirm, sign, done

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Afternoon! Delivery for Pim Suwan?
lines.th: สวัสดีตอนบ่ายครับ! พัสดุของคุณพิม สุวรรณ ใช่ไหมครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Yes, that's me.
lines.th: ใช่ค่ะ ตัวเองเลย

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Great. Two parcels today. Can you sign here, please?
lines.th: ดีครับ วันนี้มีสองกล่อง เซ็นตรงนี้หน่อยได้ไหมครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sure. Where do I sign?
lines.th: ได้ค่ะ เซ็นตรงไหนคะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Right there on the screen. Any finger's fine.
lines.th: ตรงหน้าจอนี่เลยครับ ใช้นิ้วไหนก็ได้

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Okay. Can you put the big box inside the door?
lines.th: โอเค ช่วยยกกล่องใหญ่เข้าไปวางในประตูให้หน่อยได้ไหมคะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: No worries. There you go.
lines.th: ได้เลยครับ นี่ครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Thanks a lot. Have a good one.
lines.th: ขอบคุณมากค่ะ โชคดีนะคะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Cheers, mate. Bye!
lines.th: โอเคครับ ไปก่อนนะ!

model_dialogues.label: Wrong name on the label, then a cash-on-delivery surprise

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Hi, parcel for flat forty. Is that you?
lines.th: สวัสดีครับ พัสดุของห้อง 40 ใช่คุณไหมครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, this is flat fourteen.
lines.th: ขอโทษค่ะ ที่นี่ห้อง 14 ค่ะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Fourteen? Let me check the label again.
lines.th: 14 เหรอครับ ขอดูป้ายอีกทีนะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: One four. Not four zero.
lines.th: หนึ่ง-สี่ ไม่ใช่สี่-ศูนย์ค่ะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Ah, you're right. But the name here says Nguyen. Do you know a Nguyen?
lines.th: อ๋อ ใช่จริงด้วย แต่ชื่อในนี้เขียนว่า Nguyen รู้จักคนชื่อนี้ไหมครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: That's my neighbour, I think.
lines.th: น่าจะเพื่อนบ้านค่ะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Can you take it for them? Saves me a trip up.
lines.th: รับไว้แทนเขาได้ไหมครับ ผมจะได้ไม่ต้องเดินขึ้นไปอีกรอบ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Okay, but I can't sign their name.
lines.th: ได้ค่ะ แต่เซ็นชื่อเขาแทนไม่ได้นะคะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: No, you sign your own name and I'll write 'left with neighbour'. What's your name?
lines.th: ไม่ต้องครับ เซ็นชื่อตัวเองเลย เดี๋ยวผมเขียนว่า 'ฝากไว้กับเพื่อนบ้าน' คุณชื่ออะไรครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: It's Pim. P-I-M.
lines.th: พิมค่ะ P-I-M

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Lovely. Oh — and this second one's cash on delivery. Two hundred and fifteen.
lines.th: เยี่ยมครับ อ้อ — อีกกล่องนึงเป็นแบบเก็บเงินปลายทางนะครับ สองร้อยสิบห้า

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, how much?
lines.th: ขอโทษค่ะ เท่าไหร่นะคะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Two hundred and fifteen. Card or cash?
lines.th: สองร้อยสิบห้าครับ จ่ายบัตรหรือเงินสดดีครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: I didn't order that one.
lines.th: กล่องนั้นไม่ได้สั่งค่ะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Hmm. Is it also for Nguyen?
lines.th: อืม ของคุณ Nguyen เหมือนกันหรือเปล่าครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Yes. Please don't leave it.
lines.th: ใช่ค่ะ อย่าเพิ่งวางไว้นะคะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Fair enough. I'll take it back and try again tomorrow. Can you tell them?
lines.th: โอเคครับ งั้นเอากลับไปก่อน พรุ่งนี้มาใหม่ ช่วยบอกเขาหน่อยได้ไหมครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sure. Can you leave a card?
lines.th: ได้ค่ะ ฝากใบแจ้งไว้ให้หน่อยได้ไหมคะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Here you go. Thanks for your help.
lines.th: นี่ครับ ขอบคุณที่ช่วยนะครับ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: No problem. Thanks!
lines.th: ไม่มีปัญหาค่ะ ขอบคุณค่ะ

listening_items.audio_text: Hi, it's the courier downstairs. I've got a parcel for flat fifteen — can you buzz me in?
listening_items.question: Which flat is the parcel for?

listening_items.audio_text: Sorry we missed you. Your parcel is at the front desk. Bring photo ID to collect it.
listening_items.question: Where is the parcel, and what must you bring?
listening_items.answer: At the front desk; bring photo ID.
listening_items.distractor_focus: final consonants in 'desk' and 'ID' vs 'at the door'

listening_items.audio_text: I can leave it at the door, but you'll need to confirm in the app. Otherwise you have to sign.
listening_items.question: What do you have to do if you don't confirm in the app?
listening_items.answer: You have to sign for the parcel.

listening_items.audio_text: There are three boxes on the van for you, but only two are on my list. I'll bring the third one tomorrow.
listening_items.question: How many boxes will you get today?
listening_items.answer: Two today; the third comes tomorrow.
listening_items.distractor_focus: two / three and 'boxes' plural final cluster

listening_items.audio_text: Your delivery window is between four thirty and six. The driver's name is Sam.
listening_items.question: When will the driver come?

guided_roleplay.learner_role: You are at home waiting for two parcels. The buzzer rings.
flow: Answer the intercom and confirm your name.
Correct the flat number clearly (say the digits one by one).
Tell the driver what to do: come up, wait, or leave it at the door / front desk.
Sign, and ask where to sign or whether ID is needed.
Check the label — one parcel has the wrong name. Say it isn't yours.
Agree the next step: take it back, redeliver tomorrow, or leave a card.
Thank the driver and close the conversation.
sentence_frames: I'll be down in two minutes.
Could you leave it at the door?
Sorry, could you say that again?

free_roleplay.ai_persona: A friendly but rushed delivery driver with a van double-parked outside. Speaks fast, uses short casual phrases ('No worries', 'Cheers', 'Sign here for me'), and will repeat more slowly if the learner asks.
free_roleplay.a2_behavior: Sticks to the standard sequence: confirms the name, states how many parcels, asks for a signature, accepts 'leave it at the door', says goodbye. Repeats numbers on request.
b1_curveballs: Says the wrong flat number and insists it is correct until the learner spells out the digits.
The label has a neighbour's name and the driver asks the learner to accept it on their behalf.
Announces an unexpected cash-on-delivery charge and asks 'card or cash?'.
Says one box is missing from the van and offers redelivery tomorrow or pickup at the depot.
The box is visibly damaged and the driver asks whether the learner still wants to accept it.
Refuses to leave it at the door because the item needs a signature and ID.
Is about to leave the parcel in the lobby and drive off unless the learner stops them.

roleplay_rubric.criterion: Confirmed identity and corrected/confirmed the flat or unit number so the driver repeated it back correctly
Gave a clear instruction about where to leave the parcel (door / front desk / neighbour) or came down to collect it
Handled signing: asked where to sign, or asked whether ID was needed
Refused or flagged a parcel that was not theirs instead of silently accepting it
Asked at least one clarification question ('Sorry, could you say that again?' / 'Sorry, how much?')
Pronunciation: final consonants ('sign', 'box', 'mine', 'desk') audible and -teen/-ty numbers distinguishable
Coped with the curveball (COD charge, damaged box, missing parcel) and negotiated a next step without abandoning the conversation

register_culture_note.en: Doorstep delivery talk is fast, friendly and very short. Drivers are on a timer, so full polite sentences are less useful than clear short ones: 'Yes, that's me', 'Flat fourteen', 'Where do I sign?'. Saying no is completely normal — refusing a parcel that isn't yours, or refusing an unexpected charge, is expected behaviour, not rudeness. Repeat digits one by one when a number is misheard.

do_dont.avoid: Silently taking a parcel with someone else's name on it
do_dont.prefer: Sorry, this isn't mine — wrong name.

do_dont.avoid: 'Fourteen' said with weak stress and no final /n/ (heard as 'forty')
'Put it door' (missing preposition, dropped final sounds)
do_dont.prefer: Could you leave it at the door?

do_dont.avoid: Nodding and smiling when you didn't understand the amount
do_dont.prefer: Sorry, how much? Could you say that again?

do_dont.avoid: 'You must wait me' when you need time
do_dont.prefer: I'll be down in two minutes.

do_dont.avoid: Signing for a neighbour without saying so
do_dont.prefer: I'll sign, but it's for my neighbour in fourteen B.

register_culture_note.thai_cultural_note: In Thailand it is common and low-risk for a guard, front desk or neighbour to accept parcels for you, and many learners assume the same casual arrangement applies everywhere. In many countries a signature makes you legally responsible for that item, and a COD signature means the money is owed. It is not impolite to say 'Sorry, this isn't mine' or 'Please don't leave it' — drivers hear this every day and simply mark it as refused.

can_do_checkpoints.statement: I can confirm my name and flat number at the door or on the intercom.
I can say where I want a parcel left and ask where to sign.
I can understand how many parcels are being delivered and when the driver will return.
I can refuse a parcel that isn't mine and explain why.
I can deal with a surprise — a cash-on-delivery charge, a damaged box or a missing item — and agree a next step.
My final consonants ('sign', 'box', 'mine', 'desk') are audible and my -teen/-ty numbers are not confused.

unlocks: Intercom Master — handle a buzzer call with no repeats needed
Right Flat, Right Box — correct a wrong number so the driver repeats it back correctly
Not Mine — refuse a mis-addressed parcel politely in under three turns
Curveball Survivor — complete a B1 roleplay with a COD or damaged-box twist
